papers.title: Densitometric evaluation of periprosthetic bone remodeling.
papers.abstract: The application of Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) in orthopaedic surgery gradually has been extended from the study of osteoporosis to different areas of interest like the study of the relation between bone and prosthetic implants. Aim of this review is to analyze changes that occur in periprosthetic bone after the implantation of a total hip arthroplasty (THA) or a total knee arthroplasty (TKA). In THA the pattern of adaptive bone remodeling with different cementless femoral stems varies and it appears to be strictly related to the design and more specifically to where the femoral stem is fixed on bone. Short stems with metaphyseal fixation allow the maintenance of a more physiologic load transfer to the proximal femur decreasing the entity of bone loss. Femoral bone loss after TKA seems to be related to the stress shielding induced by the implants while tibial bone remodeling seems to be related to postoperative changes in knee alignment (varus/valgus) and consequently in tibial load transfer. After both THA and TKA stress shielding seems to be an inevitable phenomenon that occurs mainly in the first year after surgery.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇综述讨论了THA后股骨假体周围的应力遮挡及骨重塑模式，但未涉及定量力学分析或有限元建模。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a qualitative clinical review with DEXA densitometry, providing no FE modeling, no contact mechanics, no quantitative stress/strain analysis in Gruen zones, and no patient-specific implant simulations.

summary_en.motivation: This review summarizes the application of DEXA in evaluating periprosthetic bone remodeling after total hip and knee arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A narrative review of clinical studies on DEXA-based densitometry changes around cementless femoral stems and tibial components.
summary_en.result: Stress shielding is inevitable, with short metaphyseal-fixation stems reducing proximal bone loss compared to standard stems.
summary_en.validation: Clinical DEXA observations from multiple studies, without direct mechanical testing or FE validation.

summary_en.motivation: To review the application of DEXA in evaluating periprosthetic bone remodeling after total joint arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A narrative review summarizing densitometric changes in THA and TKA, focusing on stem design and alignment effects.
summary_en.result: Stress shielding is inevitable; short metaphyseal-fixation stems reduce proximal femoral bone loss.
summary_en.validation: No original validation; review of existing clinical DEXA studies.
